title: Layer-counted h-BN tunnel barrier dials retention like a knob
idea: Effect walk: direct quantum tunneling through atomically defined barriers. A 2D semi-floating-gate cell (graphene or MoS2 storage layer) sits behind exactly N layers of h-BN; because direct-tunneling current drops ~10x per added 0.33-nm layer, N=4-6 sets retention near 1 s while 10-ns writes use direct (not Fowler-Nordheim) tunneling at 2-3 V that creates no oxide traps.
why: Replaces junction leakage statistics with a quantized, atomically uniform barrier, collapsing the retention tail (fact 3) and refresh energy, and needs no capacitor (fact 1); wafer-scale defect-free h-BN and the write/hold current ratio of ~10^8 are the risks.

title: Remove defects, not add capacitance: hBN-sealed 2D gain cell
idea: Reverse retention strategy from bigger capacitor to zero trap states: a WSe2 or MoS2 monolayer write transistor fully encapsulated in hBN (no dangling bonds) charges an hBN-isolated graphene storage gate, so the trap-assisted tunneling behind the 13 fA leakage tail has no sites to use.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 1.5-2 eV-gap channels with clean interfaces target <1e-19 A, i.e., minutes-to-hours retention and >100x less refresh energy; thin-film tiers stack (fact 2).

title: Barrier-free spin-orbit bit read by anomalous Hall cross
idea: MINIFY the magnetic stack to three sputtered layers with no tunnel barrier: a perpendicular Co dot on a Pt Hall cross is switched by spin-orbit torque from in-plane current and read by its anomalous Hall voltage with a differential sense amp, needing one litho step and one sputter run.
why: Unlimited magnetic endurance and nonvolatility in a process a small team owns; ~mV signal favors cache-sized arrays.

title: MNOS revival: direct-tunnel nitride-trap one-transistor cell on SONOS lines
idea: The 1967 MNOS stored charge in nitride traps behind a thin oxide. On existing 40/28-nm embedded SONOS lines, thin the tunnel oxide to ~1.5 nm so writes are pure direct tunneling at +-3 V in ~20 ns, giving hour-scale retention ('dynamic flash') without hot-carrier or FN damage.
why: 1T cell with no capacitor (Fact 1), refresh every ~10 minutes instead of 64 ms (Fact 3: ~10,000x fewer refreshes), non-destructive read; endurance projected 1e12+ because direct tunneling avoids oxide wear, still to be proven DRAM-class.

title: Crested-barrier floating node written by DRAM's existing 3 V wordline rail
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): no new supply pins, so reuse the ~3 V VPP rail DRAM already has. Store charge on a floating node behind a crested SiO2/Si3N4/SiO2 barrier whose peaked profile collapses under high field for ns writes but stays thick at hold fields for hours of retention; reads sense the storage transistor's threshold shift.
why: The existing wordline rail powers a quasi-nonvolatile 1T cell with no capacitor (facts 1, 3); endurance under repeated tunneling writes is the unknown.

title: Crimped weft capacitors: weave 3D DRAM's lateral capacitors over posts
idea: Borrow the crimp of woven cloth. In a stacked 3D DRAM tier, the horizontal capacitor is coated like a yarn (Ru core, HZO/ZrO2 sheath, TiN outer shell) and snakes over and under a comb of sacrificial vertical 'warp' posts that are removed afterward. The crimped path packs 1.3-1.6x more electrode length into the same tier footprint.
why: Fact 2: the lateral capacitor is what blocks 3D DRAM. ~1.5x Cs per cell cuts the tiers needed to break even from ~26 toward ~18.

title: Bistable buckled 2D-membrane nanodrum stores the bit as curvature
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution + #14 Spheroidality: a pre-compressed few-layer hBN or graphene membrane over a ~30-nm cavity buckles either up or down; an electrostatic pulse from the top or bottom electrode snaps it over, and its capacitance to the bottom electrode reads the state without disturbing it. No charge is stored, so nothing leaks.
why: Facts 3 and 8: zero refresh and non-destructive read; 2D membranes survive >10^12 flex cycles; back-end array over periphery at ~4F2.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate planar capacitor at 77 K
idea: MAGNIFY permittivity through quantum paraelectricity: SrTiO3 near 77 K has bulk k ~1000-1500; a strain-engineered 5-nm film on a SrRuO3 electrode that keeps k >= 300 makes a flat 20x20 nm capacitor of ~0.2-0.7 fF, enough with cryogenic retention.
why: Flat, etch-free capacitor replaces the AR 70:1 pillar (fact 1) and its litho/etch steps (fact 4); interfacial dead layer is the main risk.

title: The channel is the bit: ferroelectric-semiconductor transistor, no capacitor
idea: Merge storage and access roles into one layer: an alpha-In2Se3-type ferroelectric semiconductor forms the transistor channel itself, and its own polarization bends the band to set high or low current; there is no capacitor and no separate gate ferroelectric to fatigue.
why: Capacitor and 3D blockers (facts 1,2): 1T 4F2 thin-film cell stackable in tiers, nonvolatile so refresh disappears; risk is polarization screening by channel carriers.

title: Yuba-skimmed dielectric: peel atomically thin oxide skins off liquid metal
idea: Copy yuba (tofu-skin) making. A Ga-Hf liquid alloy grows a self-limiting HfO2-rich oxide skin ~1 nm thick, and touching a wafer to the surface prints that skin, pinhole-free, as the capacitor dielectric at near-room temperature.
why: Fact 1: a near-perfect 1 nm high-k skin gives EOT ~0.2 nm, about 3x capacitance per area for planar plates in stacked 3D tiers. The low temperature allows BEOL stacking.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops hold persistent-current bits
idea: Pair cell scale with datacenter cryogenics: NbN nanowire loops 100-200 nm across store a fluxon as circulating supercurrent with indefinite retention at 4 K, read by a nanowire cryotron; deployed in cryo pods next to superconducting accelerators.
why: Energy: zJ-class writes and no refresh; kinetic inductance shrinks the loop well below magnetic-inductance limits.

title: Bimetallic-strip negative-capacitance capacitor: ferroelectric AlBN fights linear Al2O3
idea: A thermostat's bimetallic strip pairs two opposing layers to get a new behavior. Here a wurtzite ferroelectric Al(1-x)B(x)N layer sits in series with Al2O3 dielectric, matched so the ferroelectric's negative-capacitance region is stabilized and never switches, lifting total capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.
why: Facts 1 and 10: capacitance rises 2-3x, and the charge gain lets VARY fall toward 0.6 V. Only Al, B, N and O, with no Hf or Zr.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission access to vacuum-isolated storage electrodes
idea: Invert 'the storage node must sit in solid insulator next to a semiconductor' -> put it in vacuum. Each cell is a sealed nano-cavity on glass where a sharp emitter faces the floating storage electrode across a ~20 nm vacuum channel, gated so field emission charges or discharges the node; when off, vacuum conducts nothing.
why: Removes junction leakage and its refresh (fact 3), radiation- and temperature-immune, no silicon wafer; emitter uniformity, nano-cavity sealing and ~10 V emission fields are the risks.

title: Printed vacuum nanogap access device with near-zero leakage
idea: IFR: the ideal insulator is nothing at all. Closest achievable: R2R-print electrodes and open ~10 nm nanogaps by controlled film cracking or sacrificial-layer removal, forming field-emission vacuum switches that conduct only above emission voltage, so a printed capacitor keeps its charge for hours.
why: Fact 3: leakage tail eliminated without needing a high-quality semiconductor; fully printable.

title: Expiring memory: retention sized to the data's lifetime, never refreshed
idea: AI activations, KV-cache blocks and gradients live 1-500 ms. The allocator tags each buffer with its lifetime and places it in banks whose measured cell retention exceeds that lifetime, and those banks never refresh because the data is dead before it decays.
why: Removes refresh energy and the 10-20% bandwidth loss (fact 3) for most AI traffic. Cells that only need ~100 ms retention can also use smaller capacitors (fact 1).

title: Swap oxide ferroelectric for vapor-deposited molecular ferroelectric croconic acid
idea: Use a proton-tautomerism organic ferroelectric (croconic acid, Pr ~20 uC/cm2, or DIPAB) evaporated onto the cap electrode at <150 C. It switches by proton transfer, not oxygen-vacancy motion, so HZO's vacancy-driven wake-up and fatigue are absent.
why: A low-temperature BEOL storage layer for monolithic stacking above logic, with periphery under the array (fact 7), and no rare inputs; the target is FeRAM-class endurance beyond 10^12 cycles.

title: Conducting charged domain wall in thin-film lithium niobate as bit
idea: Box = {medium: presence or absence of a conducting head-to-head domain wall in LiNbO3-on-insulator | access: Si FET in the CMOS below | sense: nondestructive wall current (on/off ~1e4) | integration: hybrid-bonded LNOI film over logic | substrate: LNOI | fab: ion slicing + e-beam-defined electrode pairs}. A ~3 V pulse between two in-plane electrodes 30 nm apart nucleates or erases a charged wall bridging them; a read only measures conduction through the wall, so polarization never reverses on read.
why: Fact 8 destructive read and Fact 3 refresh: a nonvolatile cell with nondestructive read (NDRO) avoids restore energy (~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and refresh; wall motion needs no oxygen-vacancy drift, so endurance may exceed hafnia.

title: Swap fixed capacitor for gated-diode varactor that amplifies on read
idea: Store charge in the inversion layer of a gated diode (IBM 2T1D cell). At read the gate is pulsed: a stored '1' keeps its inversion capacitance and boosts the node voltage several-fold, while a '0' collapses to depletion capacitance, which gives built-in voltage gain.
why: The signal gain lets ~1 fF planar storage work (fact 1) with only mature-node DUV (fact 4), and lowers bitline-swing energy (fact 10).

title: Glow-pigment trap bit: persistent-phosphor traps read by stimulated light
idea: Borrow glow-in-the-dark SrAl2O4:Eu,Dy pigment manufacturing. A co-packaged photonic die writes a bit by trapping electrons at Dy traps in phosphor nanodots on plasmonic antennas, and reads it by optically stimulated luminescence into an on-die SPAD. Co-dopant chemistry sets the trap depth and thus the retention.
why: Facts 5 and 3: the trap does not wear, so endurance is unlimited. Minutes of retention cut refresh ~1000x and optical read allows photonic links, but antennas limit density to ~50 nm pitch.

title: JEDEC cell-agnostic conformance badge for non-capacitor DDR5 dies
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged) turned into policy: fund a JEDEC/CHIPS conformance suite that certifies any DDR5/HBM3 die by behavior alone (timings, refresh tolerance, 1e16-write endurance stress, hammer tests) rather than by cell type, and pair it with federal procurement preference for certified second-source dies built on new storage elements.
why: Cuts the adoption barrier for new storage elements to zero controller changes and shortens qualification by years, widening supply and U.S. manufacturability.

title: Coaxial dual-node pillar stores two bits in one capacitor footprint
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): pitch and interface stay, so get more bits per pillar. Build each pillar as three concentric shells (an inner storage electrode, a shared grounded middle plate with dielectric on both faces, and an outer annular storage electrode), each storage electrode tied to its own vertical access transistor, so one footprint holds two independent ~4 fF bits.
why: Doubles capacitor area used per footprint (fact 1) with 4F2 vertical transistors underneath, ~1.5x density at the same litho (fact 4); concentric deposition in HAR holes is the risk.

title: Post-tensioned capacitor pillars that resist leaning at AR 120
idea: Borrow post-tensioned concrete: deposit a compressive inner liner and a tensile outer TiN in each pillar so residual stresses cancel bending and capillary collapse during wet clean, letting pillars reach AR ~120 without extra support lattices.
why: Fact 1: AR ~115 is what the charge wall demands; removes 1-2 support-layer modules and pattern-collapse yield loss.

title: Phase not charge: parametric-oscillator bits sustained by their own pump
idea: Turn refresh from a tax into the storage itself: each bit is a high-Q nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared row line, oscillating in one of two phases (0 or pi) that the pump keeps alive; read by phase comparison, write with a brief seed pulse (a modern Goto parametron).
why: Refresh and row hammer (facts 3,9): no static charge to leak or disturb; at Q ~1e4 the shared pump costs ~fW per bit versus 46 fJ/bit refresh; risk is resonator density (~100 nm NEMS).

title: Tunnel-diode latched storage node for always-on phone sensor hubs
idea: Phones' always-on hubs burn standby power on refresh, so two series interband tunnel diodes (Si/SiGe Esaki) form a Goto pair on each storage node, creating two stable voltages held by picoamp valley currents. The access transistor reads and writes as usual; the node simply never decays.
why: Eliminates refresh (fact 3, 16-33% idle power) with ~pA/cell standby at near-1T1C area; requires tight peak/valley current control in BEOL-compatible tunnel diodes.

title: Tesla-valve graded barrier that ratchets charge into the node
idea: Borrow the no-moving-parts Tesla fluidic diode: build a compositionally graded oxide barrier (InGaZnO to Ga2O3 to Al2O3) between access channel and storage node so the write-direction barrier collapses under field while the retention-direction barrier stays >1.5 eV.
why: Fact 3: an asymmetric barrier decouples write speed from retention, targeting ~10 ns writes with seconds of retention and ~10x fewer refreshes.

title: GaN polarization well that holds charge behind 3.4 eV walls
idea: Worsen: store charge in silicon, whose 1.1 eV gap invites thermal leakage. Flip: use a GaN-on-Si power-foundry shuttle (~$80k per run) to build AlGaN/GaN cells whose built-in polarization well stores electrons behind wide-bandgap barriers, aiming to show ~1000x lower leakage within 24 months.
why: Refresh (fact 3): hours of retention, using existing US and allied GaN fabs instead of DRAM fabs.

title: Swap litho-patterned storage nodes for area-selective bottom-up growth
idea: Use area-selective ALD/CVD (inhibitor self-assembled monolayers on the dielectric, so growth occurs only on metal landing pads) to grow TiN storage-node pillars upward from each contact. The node layer copies the DUV-made contact pattern with no lithography or etch of its own.
why: Removes one or two critical litho/etch layers (fact 4) and the high-AR etch (fact 1); the pillars are self-aligned, so there is no overlay error.

title: Bistable DX-center defect ensemble as charge store in AlGaN HEMT
idea: Box = {medium: electrons captured by DX centers (large lattice relaxation) in Si-doped high-Al AlGaN | access: the HEMT gate itself | sense: 2DEG density shift read as drain current | integration: GaN-on-Si memory tiles | substrate: GaN-on-Si | fab: MOCVD}. DX centers capture hot electrons in nanoseconds, but their lattice relaxation raises a ~0.6-1 eV emission barrier, so trapped charge stays for seconds to minutes; the defect's own physics acts as the capacitor.
why: Facts 1 and 3: a capacitorless store with engineered retention and 100x+ longer refresh intervals, using a defect normally treated as a nuisance.

title: Nanobattery bit holds voltage as chemical potential
idea: Scale an EV battery down to a 20 nm solid-state stack (Li-ion cathode/LiPON/anode): the bit is the open-circuit voltage set by tiny shallow charge swings and sensed by a gate, which holds without dielectric leakage.
why: Refresh: self-discharge is far slower than capacitor leakage, so refresh can be rare.

title: Abacus bead: electron packet shuttled between twin floating islands
idea: Stimulus 'abacus' (a bead slides, nothing is added or removed) -> each cell has two oxide-isolated floating nano-islands joined by a gated tunnel barrier; writing moves a fixed packet of ~5,000 electrons left or right, and a differential sense amp compares the two islands. Total charge is conserved, so substrate/junction leakage disappears and common-mode drift cancels while the signal doubles.
why: Doubles sense margin per stored electron, so Cs can halve (~5 fF -> ~2.5 fF), cutting pillar AR from ~70:1 to ~35:1 (fact 1) and relaxing refresh because only intra-cell differential leakage matters (fact 3).

title: Eliminate current-driven writes: magnetoelectric bismuth ferrite flips electroplated nanomagnets
idea: Eliminate write current and the tunnel junction: a BiFeO3 layer grown from solution or by PLD in O2 switches its coupled ferroelectric and antiferromagnetic order at sub-volt bias and drags an exchange-coupled electroplated CoFe nanomagnet with it; the bit is read from the CoFe's anomalous Hall voltage, so no MgO barrier or fixed layer is sputtered with argon.
why: aJ-scale writes break the CV2 floor through low voltage (fact 10), nonvolatile (fact 3), rare-gas-free stack; risks are BFO switching endurance and ns speed at scale.

title: Cu: CaCu3Ti4O12 colossal-k barrier-layer dielectric for flat capacitors
idea: Use CCTO, whose internal grain-boundary barrier layers give an apparent k of 1e3-1e4, as the cell dielectric so a planar or 5:1 capacitor reaches 5 fF; its lossy, grain-dependent leakage would doom a standard cell, but a 1% weak-cell budget plus faster refresh of flagged rows absorbs it.
why: Attacks the capacitor wall (fact 1) with ~100x k, eliminating the deep pillar etch; Ca, Cu, Ti and O are all abundant; barrier-layer response must survive ns timescales (major risk).

title: Pinned buried-well storage node copied from CMOS image sensors
idea: Store the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well pinned by a p+ surface layer, exactly like a pinned photodiode, and move it in and out through a transfer gate to a floating-diffusion read node; the stored charge never touches the Si/SiO2 interface or a contacted junction.
why: Fact 3: pinned photodiodes reach ~aA dark current per pixel; removing interface-trap generation could cut the retention tail 10-100x and refresh energy/bandwidth with it.

title: Non-contact bistable buckled nanobeam as a mechanical bit
idea: IFR: a bit held by geometry that costs nothing to keep. Closest achievable: a ~50 nm compressively prestressed SiC or graphene beam buckles up or down (two energy minima), is flipped by a ns electrostatic pulse from side electrodes and read capacitively; it never touches anything, so there is no stiction or wear.
why: Zero retention energy and no refresh (fact 3), no capacitor charge wall (fact 1); GHz-class beams switch in ~1-10 ns; endurance effectively unlimited because there is no contact.

title: Po: the capacitor is a sponge — dealloyed nanoporous storage electrode
idea: Po: the capacitor is a sponge. Extracted: deposit a TiN-Al alloy into a shallow cup, selectively dealloy the Al to leave a nanoporous TiN electrode with 5-10x surface area, then ALD-coat dielectric and top electrode through the pores (a nanoscale successor to hemispherical-grain silicon).
why: The same ~5 fF from a 10-15:1 cup instead of 60-75:1 (fact 1), cutting etch time and steps. Conformal ALD into nanopores is the risk.

title: n-i-p-i doping superlattice storing separated electrons and holes
idea: IFR: charge that can never recombine. Closest achievable: a Dohler n-i-p-i superlattice (alternating n and p doping sheets) separates electrons and holes into different layers, stretching recombination lifetimes toward seconds; many periods stack charge vertically in one cell footprint.
why: Facts 1 and 3: stored charge scales with period count (epitaxial, no high-AR etch) and retention is long.

title: Cytochrome P450 spin-switch bit held at 85C mid-hysteresis
idea: Heme enzymes like P450 flip the iron spin state when a substrate binds. Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover films have a 30-40 K wide thermal hysteresis that can be tuned to centre near the DRAM junction temperature (~85 C). Hold the die at mid-loop, write with a local 20 ns heat or field pulse, and read the 5-10% dielectric or resistance difference between the high-spin and low-spin states.
why: Removes the capacitor and refresh, because the state is bistable while the die is warm. The molecular film is solution-processed with no EUV, and die temperature becomes a resource instead of a leakage enemy.

title: Make flash leak on purpose: direct-tunnel nanocrystal storage
idea: Reverse flash's priorities: grow silicon nanocrystals on a 2 nm tunnel oxide in a 180 nm logic flow (Tiwari-style, 1996) so electrons enter and leave by direct tunneling in ~10-100 ns at +/-2-3 V with no Fowler-Nordheim damage, trading retention (seconds to hours) for near-unlimited endurance; the bit is a threshold shift read non-destructively.
why: Refresh and destructive read (facts 3,8): 1T capacitor-free cell with >=1000x DRAM retention and NDRO; risk is Vt window and endurance beyond 1e12.

title: Widrow's memistor revived: thermally gated oxide-ion bit
idea: Widrow's 1960 memistor, copper plated from a liquid electrolyte, died from slowness and liquids. Use a solid oxide-ion conductor (stabilized zirconia, Ea ~1.0-1.1 eV) between mixed-conducting electrodes, with an integrated nanoheater that takes the 20 nm cell to ~700 C during writes: ions move ~1 nm in ~100 ns when hot, while diffusion at 125 C is roughly ten orders of magnitude slower.
why: Ionic memory whose 125 C/10 y retention follows directly from high activation energy; multi-level; mostly earth-abundant Zr.

title: Deuterium isotope passivation trims the access-transistor leakage tail
idea: Scale down to the isotope: anneal in D2 instead of H2 so interface traps are capped with Si-D bonds, which resist desorption and trap-assisted tunneling more strongly over years of operation, shrinking the GIDL tail.
why: Leakage tail and refresh: if the worst tail drops 2-4x, refresh can be 2-4x rarer at 32-64 Gb; cheap drop-in.

title: Half-inch Minimal Fab runs a full 1T1C process on desks
idea: MINIFY the fab: run a planar or trench 1T1C process on 12.5-mm wafers with desk-sized Minimal Fab tools (maskless litho, per-tool local cleanroom, ~$5-20M total), so a 10-person team iterates storage-element materials in days instead of waiting for foundry lots.
why: Capital intensity ~1000x lower for R&D and small-batch defense or rad-hard memory (fact 4, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Po: the bit is a whirlpool — magnetic vortex-core polarity cells
idea: Po: the bit is a whirlpool. Extracted: in a ~50 nm permalloy disk the magnetization curls into a vortex whose 10 nm core points up or down; a GHz current pulse tuned to that disk's gyrotropic resonance flips only its core, and an MTJ over the core reads it.
why: Frequency-selective writing lets many disks of different diameters share one line, shrinking periphery (fact 7); non-volatile with fJ flips.

title: PAM-8 telecom signaling in stacked gain cells with pilot cells
idea: Borrow PAM/QAM with training symbols: hold 8 voltage levels on each oxide-semiconductor gain-cell node, write pilot cells with known levels in every row so the sense ADC tracks leakage drift, and stack 4 deposited tiers in the BEOL.
why: 10x at same cost: 3 bits/cell x 4 tiers is ~12x bits per footprint; tiers are deposited oxide layers (no EUV) and pilot-tracked thresholds tolerate drift.

title: Freestanding SrTiO3 membrane transfer gives k~300 capacitors cold
idea: Grow single-crystal SrTiO3 on a donor wafer over a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, release it in water, and transfer and bond the ~5 nm membrane onto the memory wafer at <=300 C. Crystallization happens off-wafer, so the product never exceeds 400 C yet gets a k~300 dielectric.
why: k~300 beats the k~70 that fact 1 requires, allowing 5 fF at AR ~15:1 or as a planar 3D tier. The constraint is met by moving heat off the product wafer; dead-layer k loss is the risk.

title: Po: the bit is a knot — 3D hopfion storage, chiral magnets
idea: Po: the bit is a knot that cannot untie itself. Extracted: in a thick chiral magnetic film a hopfion (3D knotted magnetization soliton) is topologically protected; bits are hopfion present/absent at pinning sites stacked through the film thickness, nucleated by local spin-orbit torque and read by MTJ.
why: Volumetric non-volatile storage without per-tier transistors (fact 2). Room-temperature hopfion stability is speculative.

title: Eliminate vacuum high-k deposition: hydrothermal conversion of titania shells to SrTiO3
idea: Eliminate ALD of exotic high-k: coat capacitor holes with a few nm of TiO2, then convert it in place in an aqueous Sr(OH)2/Ba(OH)2 bath at 150-200 C into crystalline SrTiO3 or (Ba,Sr)TiO3 (k~100-300), conformal because the ion exchange follows the TiO2 template.
why: k well above the fact-1 target of 70 lets AR fall to ~30-40; a water-based step with no plasma or rare gases cuts tool cost (fact 4); risks are leakage below 8 nm and crystallization defects.

title: Sixty-four independently biased plate segments isolate shorted capacitor blocks
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: break the array's common capacitor plate into 64 switch-fed segments per bank. A plate-to-node short, today a die-killer because the plate is shared, is isolated in the field by floating that segment and remapping its 1/64 of the bank to spare rows, so the die is repaired rather than scrapped.
why: Yield and repairability: recovers dies lost to plate shorts (est. several % yield) and keeps aging parts in service.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly patterning hexagonal capacitor arrays
idea: Combine directed self-assembly of PS-b-PMMA cylinders, which form hexagonal close-packed arrays at 20-28 nm pitch, with the DRAM capacitor array, which is already hexagonal: a coarse DUV prepattern guides the cylinders, which are transferred into a hard mask to define capacitor holes. Spin-on chemistry replaces one or two EUV or quad-patterning layers.
why: Fact 4: removes EUV from the capacitor level; ~5-8% wafer cost reduction and less dependence on the single EUV supplier.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade dot storing five electrons per bit
idea: Box = {medium: 1-10 electrons on a ~2 nm Si dot | access: tunnel barrier to a 5 nm Si nanowire channel | sense: dot charge gates the nanowire (gain read) | integration: stacked vertical nanowires | substrate: Si | fab: self-limiting thermal oxidation sculpts the dot}. The dot's ~0.3-0.5 eV charging energy blocks back-tunneling, so a few electrons hold state for seconds, and the nanowire current amplifies them for sensing.
why: Energy per bit drops to the aJ scale (Fact 10) with no capacitor (Fact 1): ~1000x less stored charge than a 5 fF cell.

title: Eliminate the pillar: quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 reaches giant permittivity at 77 K
idea: Eliminate the 3D capacitor by using temperature: SrTiO3 is a quantum paraelectric whose permittivity climbs from ~300 at room temperature to thousands near 77 K, so an LN2-cooled planar SrTiO3 capacitor grown by MOCVD or hybrid MBE (no argon) stores the ~1-2 fF that 77-K retention requires on a flat ~30 nm pad. The helium ban steers us to the one cryogen that still unlocks this.
why: Removes the AR 60-75 etch entirely (facts 1, 4) on top of the cryogenic retention gain (fact 3); risks are thin-film dead layers cutting k 5-10x and k falling under DC bias.

title: Origami scroll: self-rolling nanoscroll capacitor released by plain water
idea: Stimulus 'paper scroll' -> deposit a flat, strain-graded TiN/Al2O3/TiN stack on a water-soluble GeO2 sacrificial layer; dissolving the GeO2 in DI water (instead of HF) lets built-in strain roll the stack into a ~10-turn, ~100 nm diameter nanoscroll over its contact, giving pillar-class electrode area from planar deposition.
why: 3D capacitor area without deep high-AR etch (facts 1, 4); fluorine-free release that also avoids wet-etch pillar collapse.

title: Scanner-free cell arrays: laser interference lithography plus e-beam periphery
idea: Box = {medium: charge on pillar capacitors | access: vertical FET | sense: standard SA | integration: periodic array patterned separately from the periphery | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: 4-beam 193 nm interference exposure from U.S. lasers gives a defect-free ~68 nm pitch dot lattice, pitch-split 2-4x by ALD spacers, while a U.S. multibeam writer exposes only the irregular periphery}. Cell arrays are perfectly periodic, so they need interference, not imaging, which removes imported scanners and masks.
why: Fact 4 and the EUV chokepoint: the cell array needs no photomask or scanner, cutting lithography capex by ~10x.

title: Swap 3D NAND thick tunnel oxide for direct-tunnel volatile trap
idea: Run existing DUV 3D NAND lines with a ~1.5-2 nm direct-tunnelling oxide under the nitride trap. The cells write in ~10-50 ns at <4 V, keep data for seconds to minutes (refreshed like DRAM) and avoid Fowler-Nordheim damage, aiming at >10^14 cycles.
why: Puts 200+-layer 3D NAND capacity, which needs no EUV, to work as volatile working memory at DRAM-class density or better (facts 2, 4). The fabs and tools already exist, including in the U.S.

title: Eliminate deposited tunnel oxides: ligand shells set nanocrystal storage barriers
idea: Eliminate the deposited tunnel oxide: spin-cast monodisperse 4-nm Si or InP nanocrystals as storage nodes whose organic ligand shell (C8 vs C12 alkyl chains) is the tunnel barrier, so barrier width is fixed molecularly to ~0.1 nm and retention from ms to s is chosen by ligand length; writes tunnel in ns at ~1 V, with no vacuum tool or gas.
why: Removes ALD/PVD steps and the capacitor (fact 1), and molecularly uniform barriers collapse the retention tail (fact 3); risks are ligand degradation under repeated tunneling and film packing defects.

title: Reverse the charge wall: 50-electron bits read by single-electron transistors
idea: Instead of fighting for ~30,000 electrons in a 5 fF pillar, store ~50 electrons on a 0.01 fF planar node and move all the gain into the reader: a 3-5 nm room-temperature silicon Coulomb island coupled to the node swings its current by decades per few electrons.
why: Charge wall and capacitor process (facts 1,4): the tall capacitor vanishes (planar ~4F2 cell) and CV2 write energy drops ~100x; risks are RT single-electron uniformity and keeping 50 electrons from leaking.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina scaffold for litho-free capacitor arrays
idea: Worsen: pattern every capacitor hole with EUV and plasma etch. Flip: anodize an aluminium layer so it self-organizes into hexagonal 20-40 nm pores at >100:1 aspect ratio, ALD electrode/high-k/electrode inside the pores, and register access transistors to the natural lattice.
why: Removes litho and etch capital for the capacitor (fact 4) and reaches AR 115+ almost for free (fact 1).

title: Apollo core-rope ROM reborn as via-coupled multi-layer weight store
idea: Apollo's rope memory encoded bits as whether a sense wire threaded a core. Encode frozen AI weights as presence or absence of via stubs coupling word lines to sense lines across 8 metal-layer pairs of an existing 40-nm logic process (one custom via mask per layer); pulsing a word line induces charge only on sense lines with a stub, so there is no DC sneak path.
why: Frees DRAM/HBM now spent on immutable weights; no refresh, no capacitor; 8 planes x 4F2 at 40 nm is ~800 nm2 per bit, about DRAM's 864 nm2, at far lower capex and no EUV.

title: Potassium-filter storage node sealed by a resonant tunneling gate
idea: K+ channels pass ions near diffusion speed yet block others because the filter is energy-matched. Put the storage node behind a double-barrier hBN/graphene/hBN resonant tunneling contact: during write the gate aligns the resonant level and current flows freely. During hold the gate detunes it by >0.3 eV, and transmission drops >10^6 because of energy mismatch rather than barrier thickness, so leakage depends weakly on geometric variation.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): an energy-filtered off state could cut the <=13 fA tail 100-1000x and stretch refresh from 64 ms to seconds, saving most of the 16-33% idle refresh power.

title: Neuron first-spike latency: time-coded multilevel cell readout
idea: Neurons encode stimulus strength in their first-spike latency. Store four charge levels per cell and read by dumping the node onto a precharged line with a threshold inverter. A time-to-digital converter shared across 64 columns measures the trip time to ~10 ps, and that time sorts the levels instead of voltage-margin-limited multi-threshold sensing.
why: Density and cost per bit: 2 bits per cell (~1.8x bits per wafer), with per-row time calibration absorbing Cs variation. The storage element itself is unchanged.

title: Voltage-written magnetoelectric chromia bits grown epitaxially on sapphire
idea: Invert 'magnetic bits need current to write' -> write with voltage alone. Cr2O3 grows epitaxially on corundum sapphire; its antiferromagnetic order is reversed by an electric field in a small magnetic bias (magnetoelectric switching), and its boundary magnetization is read by anomalous Hall voltage in a 2 nm Pt overlayer.
why: Non-volatile, effectively unlimited endurance (no ion motion or barrier wear), write energy ~fJ capacitive instead of MRAM's ~100 fJ-pJ (fact 10), no silicon or tungsten; the ~307 K Neel point needs boron doping and the read signal is small.

title: Magnetoelectric BiFeO3 voltage-written magnet with TMR read
idea: Scarcity rule: no current may cross any insulator during a write. Ferroelectric switching of a BiFeO3 layer rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which exchange-couples to the CoFe free layer of an MTJ, so a ~100 mV gate pulse writes and TMR reads; charge only moves capacitively.
why: Attojoule-class nonvolatile writes (facts 3, 10) with no barrier stress; BiFeO3 fatigue and switching speed must reach 1e15 cycles and ns.

title: Fluorescent tracers encode storage-stack chemistry for automated recycling sorting
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes: dope each die's passivation with distinct carbon-dot or Mn:ZnS emission signatures that encode its storage-stack chemistry (Ru vs TiN electrodes, Hf vs Zr dielectric); shredder lines sort fragments optically into chemistry-matched streams for metal recovery.
why: Recyclability and scarce resources: higher-purity recovered Ru/Hf/Zr at low sorting cost.

title: Pyroelectric read: a nanoheater asks the domain which way it points
idea: Effect walk: pyroelectricity. A 10-nm resistive nanoheater under a ferroelectric bit warms a ~20-nm volume by ~10 K for 2 ns (~0.2 fJ); the polarization-dependent pyro-current, whose sign is the bit, charges the aF sense gate of a gain transistor, so the domain is read without being switched or rewritten.
why: Replaces switch-and-restore reads and full bitline swings (facts 8, 10) with ~0.2-1 fJ of heat, ~10x below DRAM read energy per bit; the signal is only a few electrons, so sensing noise is the risk.

title: Insulating garnet racetracks shift magnetic domains without Joule heating
idea: Invert 'magnetic memory needs metallic magnets on silicon' -> use an insulating ferrimagnet. Thulium-iron-garnet nanowires, sputter-crystallized on glass or grown on garnet, carry dozens of domains each, driven at >1 km/s by spin-orbit torque from a Pt underlayer, so one read/write junction per track replaces one access transistor per bit.
why: 32-64 bits per access device shrinks periphery and raises density (fact 7); non-volatile, unlimited endurance and 10-100x lower damping than metal magnets; domain-position errors and gadolinium in GGG substrates (favor glass) are the risks.

title: Recirculating acoustic delay-line memory on US BAW filter fabs
idea: Adapt 5G BAW/FBAR filter technology: launch 20 GHz phonon pulse trains into a folded AlScN waveguide loop with an on-loop regenerative amplifier, so bits circulate like mercury delay-line memory and are tapped at a known phase.
why: US manufacturability and scarce resources: runs on non-EUV, US-owned BAW fabs with no capacitor or tungsten; ~50 ns average latency, but density is low, so it suits buffer roles.

title: Prestressed magnetoelectric bit: tempered-glass stress makes strain-switched magnets bistable
idea: Copy tempered and prestressed glass: build a permanent biaxial stress into a Terfenol-D (TbDyFe) nanomagnet on a PMN-PT piezo pillar. The prestress creates two stable easy axes at +/-45 degrees, and a voltage pulse strains the magnet from one to the other. A tunnel junction reads it.
why: Fact 10: written by voltage with no current, at ~1 aJ instead of fJ-scale CV2. Nonvolatile, so refresh energy disappears.

title: Spin-crossover molecules switch between high and low spin
idea: Scale down to one Fe(II) complex: spin-crossover molecules with wide room-temperature thermal hysteresis toggle high-spin and low-spin by field pulses, changing junction conductance by 10x.
why: Density: molecular-scale bits self-assembled in crossbars without lithography.

title: Swap capacitor for vertical gated thyristor bistable latch
idea: A vertical p-n-p-n silicon thyristor with a gated base holds the bit regeneratively: latched on or blocked off, with gate pulses giving ns switching (the T-RAM/VLT lineage). It is built at 4F2 with F = 28-40 nm using DUV double patterning.
why: Static, capacitor-less storage (fact 1) with no refresh (fact 3). Because the device is vertical it can be stacked, and two tiers roughly match the bit density of EUV 6F2 at F = 12 nm without EUV (fact 4).

title: Electrolytic-capacitor 'forming': self-healing anodic Al2O3 kills leakage tail
idea: Copy the forming step of aluminum electrolytic capacitors: each cell has an anodic Al2O3 dielectric under a conductive polymer (PEDOT: C, H, O, S) counter electrode. A periodic forming voltage re-anodizes weak spots, and the polymer over hot spots de-dopes into an insulator, so leaky outlier cells cure themselves instead of setting the refresh rate.
why: Fact 3: refresh is set by the worst ~ppm leakage tail. Self-healing compresses that tail ~10x (refresh 64 ms -> ~0.5 s) using Al and organics only.

title: Age-adaptive cells step down from multi-level to binary storage
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: store 2 bits per capacitor (4 charge levels sensed against a ramped reference) while the array is young; as retention tails widen, the controller re-formats aging pages to 1 bit/cell with large margin, and later to a refresh-heavy cold tier, rather than failing the module.
why: Density ~2x early in life and ~2-3x longer service life through graceful downgrade.

title: Eliminate the access transistor: ALD tunnel-diode crossbar storage capacitors
idea: Eliminate the transistor: put each storage capacitor at a crossbar intersection behind an asymmetric metal-insulator-metal tunnel diode (ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5/TiO2 nanolaminate with barrier heights tuned for a >1e8 current ratio between 1.5 V and 0.3 V), so half-selected cells see too little bias to leak; lines are ALD TiN plus electroplated Cu, with no argon sputtering, and the 4F2 cell stacks in 8+ BEOL layers.
why: A stacked 4F2 crossbar attacks density and capital (facts 2, 4) and removes the leaky transistor; risk is holding diode leakage near fA, or refresh returns at a slower rate.

title: Memristor without filaments: conducting ferroelectric domain walls in LiNbO3
idea: HPE's TiO2 memristor died from random oxygen-vacancy filaments that caused variability, sneak paths and ~1e6-1e9 endurance. Replace the filament with a charged, conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa: writing nucleates or erases the wall deterministically at a lithographic edge, and a sub-coercive read senses wall conduction between side electrodes without moving it.
why: Deterministic, non-destructive read; endurance >1e12 because no ions migrate; ~1e3 on/off. Attacks destructive read (Fact 8) and refresh (Fact 3).

title: Conducting domain-wall bit in thin lithium niobate mesas
idea: Scarcity rule: the sense path may use no stored charge at all. A 10 nm LiNbO3 mesa either contains or lacks a charged conducting domain wall bridging two side electrodes; an in-plane voltage pulse injects or erases the wall, and read is its nA-level current, a nondestructive resistive read.
why: 2-terminal, ns-write, nondestructive read (fact 8) at low voltage on a thin-film LiNbO3 platform growing for photonics; endurance and sub-20 nm scaling are unproven.

title: Ultra-wide-bandgap Ga2O3 or diamond access transistor locks charge
idea: Combine power-electronics materials with the DRAM cell: a thin-film beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) or hydrogen-terminated diamond access transistor built in BEOL has thermal-generation and band-to-band leakage far below 1e-21 A, so a 1-5 fF node keeps its charge for years. Bits are written like DRAM and held like flash, with unlimited endurance because nothing tunnels through an oxide.
why: Fact 3: refresh power goes to zero and 10-20% bandwidth returns; goes past IGZO's ~3.2 eV gap that prior work studied.

title: Lab-grown-gem diamond storage node: 5.5 eV bandgap kills leakage tail
idea: Borrow CVD gem growth to make single-crystal diamond tiles (carbon only). The storage node is a boron-doped diamond junction capacitor with a hydrogen-terminated diamond access FET, and intrinsic carrier generation is ~1e-36 of silicon's, so retention runs to hours.
why: Fact 3: the <=13 fA leakage tail drops to effectively zero, removing the 16-33% of idle power and 10-20% of bandwidth that refresh costs. Diamond is pure carbon, and CVD reactors are small and buildable in the U.S.

title: DX centers rescued: deep-defect bistability in Si-doped AlN
idea: Persistent-photoconductivity DX-center memories in AlGaAs died because the capture barrier (~0.2-0.3 eV) held states only below ~100 K. In AlN:Si or beta-Ga2O3:Si some calculations put the DX configurational barrier near 1 eV, so an ensemble of ~1000 DX centers in a gate layer could be toggled between shallow-donor and negatively charged DX states by hot-electron injection, shifting a transistor threshold that holds at 125 C.
why: A new charge-plus-lattice-relaxation storage mode with no oxide-trap wear; nonvolatile at Grade 1 for a dense gain-cell variant.

title: Bits travel to the sensor: CMOS bucket-brigade loop memory
idea: Worsen: give every bit its own transistor, contact and wire so periphery and contacts eat the die. Flip: store bits as charge packets in buried-channel CCD potential wells clocked around short 256-bit loops with one sense and regeneration stage per loop; no per-cell transistor, contact or capacitor etch, so a cell is ~2-4F2 of gate electrodes.
why: Density and capital (no high-AR capacitor, fewer EUV contact layers, fact 4) and a smaller periphery share (fact 7); latency held under ~100 ns by many short parallel loops.

title: Bucket brigade: 64-cell charge-packet loops replace per-cell transistors
idea: A firefighter's bucket line delivers water without a pipe to every house. Store bits as charge packets marching around short CCD-style loops of 64 gate electrodes clocked at 4 GHz, with one sense/regenerate tap per loop. Worst-case access is ~16 ns, and every lap refreshes the charge for free.
why: Removes the per-bit access transistor and its leakage tail (fact 3) and shrinks the periphery (fact 7); a cell is just gates (~4F²) with no high-AR capacitor (fact 1).

title: Topological polar vortex chirality as an unleakable bit
idea: Worsen: hold bits as fragile scalar charge that any trap can steal. Flip: encode the bit as the handedness (left or right chirality) of a polar vortex or polar skyrmion in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices, switched by a sub-volt field pulse with an in-plane bias and read by tunneling resistance or piezo-current; topology protects the state at ~10 nm size.
why: Density (sub-10 nm bits, no capacitor) and refresh elimination; the topological barrier gives non-volatility without diffusion-driven fatigue.

title: Eliminate deposition-plus-etch: patternable metal-oxo resist becomes the capacitor dielectric
idea: Eliminate separate dielectric deposition and etch: coat a Hf- or Zr-oxo-cluster photoresist, expose it with 365-nm UV LEDs or e-beam (no excimer laser), develop it, and anneal the remaining pattern into dense HfO2/ZrO2 that stays in place as storage dielectric and node isolation, so the resist is the device.
why: Removes ~3-4 process steps per cell layer (fact 4 capital) and the neon-dependent ArF exposure; risk is the density and leakage of resist-derived oxide vs ALD.

title: Eliminate refresh with liquid-nitrogen cooling instead of helium cryogenics
idea: Eliminate refresh and the tall capacitor by running DRAM at 77 K, cooled with liquid nitrogen (an air-separation product, not helium): junction and GIDL leakage fall by >1e6, retention goes from 64 ms to hours, and Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~1-2 fF, a planar or AR-15 capacitor. Rack-level LN2 immersion loops use no rare gas at any step.
why: Removes refresh power (16-33% of idle, fact 3), wire resistance falls ~5x (fact 5), and the smaller capacitor drops the AR-75 etch (fact 1); the helium ban pushes cooling to N2, the cheapest cryogen; cooling overhead is offset by lower power.

title: Eliminate full magnetization reversal: single skyrmion presence-absence in nanodots
idea: Eliminate full magnetization reversal: in a 20-nm Co/Pt/Ir multilayer dot with strong DMI, the bit is the presence or absence of one skyrmion, nucleated or annihilated by a voltage-controlled-anisotropy pulse and read through noncollinear magnetoresistance in a vertical tunnel stack.
why: ~10x lower write current than STT-MRAM, nonvolatile (fact 3) and dense; risk is thermal stability of 20-nm skyrmions at room temperature.

title: Po: the bit is a spinning top — on-chip parametron phase memory
idea: Po: the bit is a spinning top. Extracted: each bit is a nonlinear LC or NEMS resonator pumped at 2f by a shared clock; it rings at f locked to phase 0 or pi, the phase is the bit, and readout compares it against a reference, so nothing sits as static charge that can leak.
why: Removes leakage-driven refresh and destructive read (facts 3, 8); energy set by resonator Q rather than CV2 at 1 V (fact 10). Resonator area/density is the main risk.

title: Two-terminal threshold-switch gated capacitors in crosspoint arrays on glass
idea: Invert 'every capacitor needs a three-terminal access transistor' -> gate it with a two-terminal ovonic threshold switch. A GeSe-class OTS in series with each MIM capacitor stays off below ~1.5 V and snaps on in <1 ns above it, forming a stackable 4F^2 1S1C crosspoint built at low temperature on glass, foil or ceramic.
why: Removes the access transistor (facts 2, 4) so tiers stack like 3D crosspoint without crystalline silicon; OTS off-current must reach ~fA or retention collapses to milliseconds, and threshold drift limits endurance.

title: Selector-only chalcogenide: threshold-voltage polarity stores the bit
idea: A single RT-sputtered GeAsSe ovonic threshold switch is both selector and memory. A write pulse of one polarity shifts its threshold voltage by ~1 V through field-driven defect and ion redistribution without crystallizing, and the read uses the opposite polarity.
why: Removes the separate storage layer, giving a one-layer 4F2 cross-point stackable at <=350 C, with no melt (energy, endurance beyond PCM) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Single reticle exposed twice rotated forms OTS-selected cross-point capacitors
idea: Hyperscale AI wants density but allows one new mask, so a lines-and-spaces reticle is exposed once for rows and again rotated 90 degrees for columns, patterning a BEOL cross-point of ovonic-threshold-switch plus MIM capacitor stacks at 4F2. The switch's steep sub-threshold cut-off isolates each capacitor, and further decks reuse the same reticle.
why: Stackable 4F2 BEOL DRAM tiers (facts 2, 4) with no new transistors and one reticle; OTS leakage at half-select bias sets retention to us-ms, the key physics risk.

title: Child's rattle: off-centre ion bit inside Li@C60 cages
idea: A child shakes a rattle and hears where the bead is. In an endohedral Li@C60 molecule the Li+ ion sits off-centre in one of two stable sites; a field pulse flips it to the other site, giving a ~1 nm molecular dipole bit that is read as a capacitance change on a gate.
why: Molecule-scale ultimate density with no leakage path, because the ion is caged (facts 1, 3).

title: Plasma-display wall-charge memory with global sustain self-refresh
idea: Adapt AC plasma panels, whose cells remember via wall charge: store the bit as charge on a dielectric wall across a 10 nm vacuum nanogap; a chip-wide AC sustain pulse makes only charged cells field-emit and re-deposit their charge, so refresh needs no row activation or sense amps.
why: Fact 3 and 7: the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss goes to ~0, refresh energy is spent only on 1-cells, and refresh periphery disappears.

title: Li-ion battery staging quantizes multi-level ionic storage
idea: Borrow graphite intercalation staging, where ions order into discrete stages with flat voltage plateaus: intercalate protons into few-layer MoS2/graphene hosts so each node rests on one of four stage plateaus read by open-circuit potential, in 3 stacked tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: plateau-quantized 2 bits/node robust to small self-discharge, x3 tiers, x~1.7 smaller node with no capacitor, ~10x.

title: Self-assembled BaTiO3 nanocube ink as a spin-coated high-k
idea: MAGNIFY permittivity by printing it: hydrothermally synthesized 10-15 nm single-crystal BaTiO3 nanocubes self-assemble from ink into dense superlattices on the bottom electrode, then an ALD infill densifies the film without high-temperature sintering, targeting k ~100-200.
why: k well above 70 (fact 1) without perovskite MOCVD/ALD capital; the low-k infill in series is the risk.

title: Toothpaste without fluoride: hydroxyapatite OH-column dipole order stores bits
idea: Stimulus 'fluoride toothpaste', inverted -> use hydroxyapatite (the fluoride-free tooth mineral) thin films, whose columns of OH- ions can order head-to-tail into a polar state; a field pulse reverses the OH column orientation, read as a polarization or capacitance change. Calcium phosphate comes from Florida phosphate rock.
why: Earth-abundant, U.S.-sourced nonvolatile polar storage layer (scarce-resource axis) with low switching voltage from proton/OH reorientation (fact 10).

title: Po: memory sold by the kilogram — volumetric electron-trapping crystal
idea: Po: memory sold by the kilogram. Extracted: a cm3 crystal or glass doped with deep electron traps (SrS:Eu,Sm or Ce-doped glass) stores bits as trapped electrons in voxels written by two-photon absorption where beams cross, read by infrared-stimulated luminescence and rewritten to refresh, with zero lithography.
why: Bulk crystal at cents per GB with TB per cm3 possible, far beyond 100x cheaper. Trade-offs: us page latency, laser/optics cost, read fading; serves as a capacity tier behind small DRAM.

title: Nanomechanical parametron stores bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's 1954 parametron at nanoscale and GHz: a doubly clamped SiC beam pumped at twice its resonance oscillates in one of two phases (0 or pi), which is the bit; the pump sustains it every cycle and neighboring beams couple to shift data.
why: Endurance and leakage: no charge to leak and no wear-out; logic and memory share one element.

title: Skyrmion racetrack in synthetic antiferromagnet tubes
idea: Scale bits down to 10 nm topological spin whirls: compensated synthetic-antiferromagnet skyrmions have no Hall drift and move at km/s, so a vertical racetrack tube stores 64 bits per access device.
why: Density and periphery: one access device per 64 bits instead of per bit, 3D vertical tubes.

title: Spin-crossover molecular film stores bits in iron's spin state
idea: Effect walk: thermal hysteresis of spin crossover. A 5-nm film of an Fe(II)-triazole coordination polymer with a 20-40 K hysteresis loop straddling room temperature forms the dielectric of a small capacitor; a short heat or field pulse flips low-spin and high-spin, changing permittivity and volume ~10%, read as a capacitance difference with a small AC probe.
why: A bistable molecular state needs no refresh and no high-AR capacitor; solution-deposited BEOL layers stack without EUV (fact 4) and use only iron, carbon and nitrogen, no chokepoint materials; switching speed and cycling endurance are unproven at ns scale.

title: Printed magnetoelectric composite written by voltage, not current
idea: IFR: magnetic bits written with zero current. Closest achievable: print magnetostrictive CoFe2O4 nanoparticles in piezoelectric P(VDF-TrFE); a voltage strains the matrix and rotates particle magnetization between two easy axes, read by a printed magnetoresistive sensor line.
why: Nonvolatile, write energy is just the CV^2 of a printed capacitor (fact 10), unlimited magnetic endurance; R2R printable.
